node Fixture.Kinds.Color.doc: An enumeration with derived instances: each deriving handler writes declarations.

node Fixture.Kinds.HasSize.doc: A class, and one that extends it.

node Fixture.Kinds.Point3.doc: A structure that extends another: its parent projection is generated.

node Fixture.Kinds.Vec.length.type: {α : Type} → {n : Nat} → Fixture.Kinds.Vec α n → Nat

node Fixture.Kinds.evenW.doc: Mutual well-founded recursion: even. Both bodies go into one generated `_mutual`.

node Fixture.Kinds.instHasSizeColor.doc: An anonymous instance: its name is made by Lean.

node Fixture.Kinds.length_nil.doc: A statement resting on several of the above.

node Fixture.Kinds.log2.doc:
Well-founded recursion: Lean generates the unary function, the induction principle and the
equation lemmas.

node Fixture.Kinds.ping.doc: Mutual partial functions: each one's code calls the other's `_unsafe_rec`.

node Fixture.Kinds.point3_size.doc: The statement rests on the parent's definitions through the projection.

node Fixture.Kinds.secret.doc: An opaque constant: a statement can rest on it, its value is not known.

node Fixture.Kinds.visible.doc: Uses the private helper in its body.

node Fixture.Pos.doc: A positive number: a `by` in a signature is the statement's, never cut.

node Fixture.Sized.doc: A type reaches what its constructor's fields do: here the open proof, through `succSize`.

node Fixture.bounded.doc: Data whose invariant is proved by a lemma: the lemma sits in a proof position.

node Fixture.classify.doc: Defined by pattern matching, so it owns a matcher.

node Fixture.commandTagged_.doc:
`tagged T` declares `T` and, beneath it, the inductive `T.Tag` it is made of and a lemma about
it. Only `T` has a name in the text: the others are made with names of their own (`mkIdent`), so
their selection range is the whole command. The lemma's proof rests on the axiom `bad`, which
nothing written in the text mentions.

node Fixture.elabTrip.doc: The elaborator of `trip!`, written as a declaration with an attribute.

node Fixture.firstPlus.doc: A `by` in the middle of a term, on two lines.

node Fixture.firstTag.doc: Uses the generated type by its constructor: the reference is one to the unit `Pair`.

node Fixture.four_mul.doc: Written with `quad!` in its proof only.

node Fixture.fromFalse.doc: Data by dot notation on a proof: the proof's name is not cut out of the name.

node Fixture.helper.doc: A helper used only inside a proof.

node Fixture.instDecidableEqPoint.doc: Equality of points decided by hand: an instance of a class whose instances are all equal.

node Fixture.main_thm.doc: The statement mentions `double` and `Point.size`; the proof uses `helper_eq`.

node Fixture.onePos.doc: A structure instance with a `by` field.

node Fixture.origin.doc: A default point: `Inhabited` carries data, its default value, so its instance stays.

node Fixture.picked.doc: Only the numeral rule of `pick!` runs, in a `by` block whose goal is data.

node Fixture.quadruple.doc: Written with `quad!` in its body: `dbl!` comes from the rule of `quad!`, not from here.

node Fixture.same.doc:
Whether two points are the same: the instance it decides with is left out of its TCB, as a
proof is.

node Fixture.size_comm.doc: An honest statement with a proof from `bad`.

node Fixture.size_twice.doc: Reaches `bad` only through the proof of `size_comm`, which it uses in its own proof.

node Fixture.sized.doc: Written with a `notation`, which bundles its syntax and its rule.

node Fixture.square.doc: An elaborated notation in a body.

node Fixture.succSize.doc: Data whose invariant is the open `size_succ_pos`, in a proof position.

node Fixture.succSize_val.doc: The statement mentions `succSize`, which mentions `size_succ_pos` only inside a proof.

node Fixture.termPick!_.doc: `pick! x`: two rules, the later tried first.

node Fixture.termPick!_.macro_rules_2.doc: The rule for a numeral, `n + 1`: it fires on numerals, and passes anything else to the first.

node Fixture.termQuad!_.doc: `quad! x` is `dbl! (dbl! x)`: its rule emits another notation of the project.

node Fixture.termWrap!_.doc:
`wrap! x` elaborates `x` after expanding the macros in it by hand: the rules that run inside
leave no trace in the info tree, only in the text.

node Fixture.three.doc: A `by` block that is data, with data and a proof nested in it.

node Fixture.tripStx.doc: `trip! x` is `3 * x`, elaborated by a declaration registered for its kind.

node Fixture.tripled.doc: Written with a syntax whose elaborator is a declaration registered for it.

node Fixture.twiceOf.doc: A meta helper: the rule of `dbl!` calls it.

node Fixture.withK.type: {α : Type} → [Inhabited α] → Nat → α → α × Nat

node Fixture.wrapped.doc: `dbl!` inside `wrap!`: the rule of `dbl!` runs in the hand expansion, and only the text says so.

node Fixture.«term‖_‖ₚ».doc: `‖p‖ₚ` is `p.size`, with an unexpander that prints it back: it only changes how a term shows.

node FixtureModule.helper.doc: A helper: in a module, a declaration is private unless made public.

node FixtureModule.triple.doc: An exposed definition: its body is exported too.

node FixtureModule.viaHelper.doc: A public definition whose body, not exported, uses the private helper.

node FixtureModule.viaHelper_eq.doc: A public theorem whose statement rests on `viaHelper`, and through its body on `helper`.
